The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
A string is wound symmetrically around a circular rod. The string goes exactly 4 times around the rod. The circumference of the rod is 4 cm and its length is 12 cm.

[Image: A cylinder with a string wound around it 4 times]

Find the length of the string. Show all your work.

Figure, described in words:
A side-view illustration of a horizontal cylindrical rod. A thick, dark line representing a string begins near the top-left edge, winds around the rod symmetrically making 4 complete helical turns from left to right, and terminates near the top-right edge.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Work: Unroll the rod into a flat rectangle. Its width is the circumference, 4 cm, and its height is the rod's length, 12 cm. The string makes 4 equal turns along the 12 cm length, so each turn rises 12 ÷ 4 = 3 cm while going 4 cm around. Each turn is therefore the diagonal of a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle, with length √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 cm. The total length of string is 4 turns × 5 cm = 20 cm. Answer: the string is 20 cm long.
